title: Graph memory compared with caption memory
description: What the current literature can—and cannot—establish about long-term video understanding.

report.question: Does structured graph memory outperform simple caption memory for long-term video memory? Cite the exact sources and the benchmark, model and subset behind every number.
report.reasoning: The provided evidence does not contain a direct head-to-head comparison between structured graph memory and simple caption memory for long-term video memory. Consequently, it is not possible to determine whether structured graph memory outperforms simple caption memory based solely on the available text.

agents.name: Researcher A
agents.summary: Direct comparisons between structured graph memory and caption-based memory for video and dialogue tasks show that structured representations generally improve reasoning and retrieval performance. On the ZH-4O benchmark, TELEMEM (using structured semantic trajectories) outperforms Mem0. Additionally, multimodal memory approaches that incorporate structured visual or textual features tend to surpass unstructured text-only caption baselines.

agents.name: Researcher B
agents.summary: Structured graph memory systems such as WorldMM achieve high performance on video QA and long-term memory benchmarks, though comparative evaluations like TELEMEM demonstrate that effectiveness depends heavily on structured representations and read-write model capacities. While explicit multimodal memory architectures improve extraction and reasoning over long horizons, simpler baselines and specific benchmarks show varying performance trade-offs.

agents.name: Contradiction Hunter
agents.summary: The provided evidence discusses various long-term video and conversational memory architectures such as WorldMM, TELEMEM, AMEGO, and M3-Agent, alongside benchmarks like ZH-4O, LoCoMo, and the Active Memories Benchmark. While structured knowledge representations and adaptive retrieval frameworks generally improve long-horizon reasoning and token efficiency, the evidence does not provide a direct head-to-head comparison between structured graph memory and simple caption memory for long-term video memory.
